# Allergy and autoimmune diseases

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Allergy and autoimmune diseases** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Human Health and Diseases fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Allergy and autoimmune diseases

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

The immune system can fail in two opposite directions. **Allergy** is an over-reaction to a harmless antigen (pollen, dust, food) — IgE-coated mast cells dump histamine. **Autoimmunity** is the loss of self-tolerance: the immune system attacks the body's own tissues (rheumatoid arthritis, Type 1 diabetes). One is an attack on something harmless; the other on something that is self.

**Concept flow — the two failures of recognition (study in this order)**

| Step | Concept | Key event |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Normal tolerance | Self-reactive lymphocytes deleted or silenced in development |
| 2 | Allergy: false alarm | IgE made against a harmless allergen; mast cells armed |
| 3 | Re-exposure → degranulation | Histamine, serotonin released → symptoms |
| 4 | Anaphylactic shock (extreme allergy) | Whole-body histamine → airway constriction, BP collapse; adrenaline is the rescue drug |
| 5 | Autoimmunity: wrong target | Self-tolerance breaks; immune attack on own organs |
| 6 | Management | Allergy: antihistamines, avoid allergen; autoimmunity: immunosuppression |

**Allergy vs autoimmune disease — classified comparison**

| Feature | Allergy | Autoimmune disease |
|---|---|---|
| Target | Harmless external antigen (allergen) | The body's own cells and tissues |
| Immune players | IgE antibodies on mast cells | Autoantibodies and self-reactive T cells |
| Mediator | Histamine, serotonin from mast cell granules | Chronic inflammation, tissue destruction |
| Onset | Minutes after exposure | Slow, chronic, relapsing |
| Common examples | Hay fever, asthma, eczema, peanut allergy | Rheumatoid arthritis, Type 1 diabetes, Graves' disease, lupus, multiple sclerosis |
| Treatment logic | Antihistamines, adrenaline for shock, avoidance | Immunosuppressant drugs; replace what is lost (insulin) |

**Major autoimmune diseases — what is attacked and the result**

| Disease | Target attacked | Main result |
|---|---|---|
| Rheumatoid arthritis | Joint lining (synovium) | Painful, swollen, deforming joints |
| Type 1 (insulin-dependent) diabetes | Insulin-producing beta cells of pancreas | No insulin → high blood sugar, insulin injections for life |
| Graves' disease | TSH receptor on thyroid | Overactive thyroid — hyperthyroidism, eye protrusion |
| Systemic lupus erythematosus | Widespread nuclear antigens | Multi-organ inflammation; skin, joints, kidneys |
| Multiple sclerosis | Myelin sheath of neurons | Slowed nerve signals — weakness, vision problems |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example.** A teenager wheezes every spring and a skin-prick test raises a red weal within minutes for grass pollen. Mechanism: first exposures made IgE against pollen; the IgE now sits on mast cells in the airway; each spring the allergen bridges two IgE molecules, the mast cell degranulates, and histamine causes bronchoconstriction. Treatment: antihistamine blocks receptors; inhaled steroids calm the chronic inflammation; adrenaline is reserved for anaphylaxis.

**Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Define allergy and name the antibody and mediator involved (IgE, histamine). (2) Why is anaphylactic shock dangerous and which drug rescues? (3) Define autoimmunity and give two diseases with the tissue attacked. (4) Contrast allergy and autoimmunity in four points. (5) Which immune failure is an over-reaction and which a loss of tolerance?

**Summary.** Allergy = IgE + mast cells + histamine aimed at a harmless target; autoimmunity = tolerance lost, self attacked. Both are failures of recognition, in opposite directions. **Self-check:** can you name the antibody in allergy and the destroyed cells in Type 1 diabetes?

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Allergy = exaggerated IgE response to harmless antigens (pollen, dust); chemicals histamine and serotonin cause sneezing, watery eyes, rashes — name the chemicals.
Trick 2: Treatment: antihistamines (cetrizine), adrenaline for anaphylaxis — the two drugs to quote.
Trick 3: Autoimmunity: immune system attacks SELF (memory loss of self-tolerance) — rheumatoid arthritis, type-1 diabetes, lupus; quote two.
Trick 4: Hereditary angle: allergies run in families (atopy) — the genetic susceptibility line.
